tex_content.html:
\begin{example} \end{example}[conjugate points in $S^n_K$]

Source: petersen:page-0273

1. ch6:6.4.5On $S^n_K$, $K>0$, polar coordinates around $p$ give $dr^2+\operatorname {sn}_K^2(r)\, d\sigma _{n-1}^2$; at distance $\pi /\sqrt K$ from $p$, every direction hits a conjugate point.

The formalized content is the analytic core: $\operatorname {sn}_K$ solves the Jacobi equation $\ddot x+Kx=0$, and $\pi /\sqrt K$ is its first positive zero (its full zero set being $\{ n\pi /\sqrt K\} $), so the sphere directions of the polar form degenerate exactly there and nowhere earlier — which is what ``every direction hits a conjugate point at distance $\pi /\sqrt K$'' says. The companion fact $\operatorname {sn}_K(t)\ne 0$ for $t>0$ when $K\le 0$ is the analytic content of section 4 (no conjugate points in nonpositive curvature). \end{example}
